decisions.executionNote: Approach the two rear upright supports with open grippers, using smooth elbow-up motion; final alignment will use wrist views.
Align to rear blocks using the calibrated head view, lowering gradually with yaw adjusted to their long axes.
Correct wrist-image centering, close both grippers fully, and make a short vertical lift to check retention.
Both blocks remain visible between the fingers. Carry them inward and square their yaw over the two lower-support positions, keeping clearance above the table.
Lower both supports onto the table, compensating the small fore-aft grasp offsets, then open the fingers without lateral motion.
Lift clear of the released supports, then spread and rotate the wrists toward a symmetric two-handed board grasp.
Finish squaring both wrists to the long lower board, then approach its ends from above while leaving the two supports untouched.
Replan from the interrupted pose with half-sized wrist rotations to preserve joint continuity, then begin a cautious board approach.
Use wrist-image centering to correct the board's fore-aft alignment, then descend slowly to grasp opposite ends.
Close both grippers on the board ends and lift together, keeping the board level before moving over the supports.
Carry the retained lower board level over the two supports, then begin a slow centered descent.
Seat the lower board gently across the two supports, open both grippers, then withdraw slightly to check stability.
The lower board appears stable with open grippers. Clear it vertically and turn toward the two remaining white blocks for the middle supports.
Approach each remaining white block from its own side, matching the visible block yaw with small continuous wrist rotations.
Refine block alignment from both wrist views and descend slowly with open fingers to the white-block grasp height.
Center the white blocks between the fingers, close fully, and lift a short distance to verify retention visually before transporting.
Both white blocks remain between the fingers. Lift above the lower board and carry inward while squaring their yaw for the middle support layer.
Center the two middle supports symmetrically over the lower board and descend together, keeping the blocks upright and grippers closed.
Seat and release both middle supports on the lower board, then lift away without dragging the blocks.
Withdraw from the upright middle supports and move toward the shorter board, rotating both wrists gradually for an end grasp.
Square both grippers over the shorter board and lower to a pregrasp height; the middle supports remain upright and clear.
Correct the shorter board's lateral offset in both wrist views and descend slowly to grasp its two ends.
Close both grippers on the shorter board and lift it level above the height of the middle supports, checking retention before translating.
Carry the retained middle board level over the upright supports, maintaining clearance and symmetric gripper spacing.
Lower the middle board slowly onto both supports while keeping it level and centered; retain the grasp until it is seated.
Open and withdraw from the seated middle board, keeping both wrists clear so its stability and the remaining top pieces can be checked.
Approach the small tan top board with the left arm, matching its visible long axis; retract the unneeded right arm along a gradual elbow-up path.
Complete the left-wrist alignment above the tan board and start a controlled descent; continue retracting the right arm away from the tower.
Refine the tan board's centering from the left wrist image and lower toward grasp height, while finishing the right arm's return toward origin.
Center and square the tan board in the left fingers, close fully, and make a short lift to verify that it is retained.
The tan board remains centered between the left fingers. Lift it clear of the tower and begin rotating its long axis across the middle board.
Carry the tan board above the tower center and finish squaring its long axis with the middle board, maintaining vertical clearance.
Lower the tan top board gently onto the middle board, with a small centering correction while keeping it upright and gripped.
Release the centered tan board, lift clear of the stack, and begin moving toward the remaining green top piece.
Move the left gripper toward a high pregrasp beside the green top piece, keeping the completed layers undisturbed and the right arm at rest.
Use the green piece's wrist-image position to shift the left wrist outward and descend, with a small yaw correction to its base edges.
Correct the green piece's yaw from the wrist view, compensate the fingertip offset, then close and lift slightly to check retention.
The green piece is retained between the fingers. Lift it well above the tower and square its base yaw before carrying it to the top board.
Carry the retained green top piece horizontally above the tan board, preserving its upright orientation and clearance from the completed layers.
Use the head view to correct the green piece slightly toward the tower center while lowering it slowly toward the tan top board.
Settle the green piece on the tan board, open the gripper, and withdraw upward and left to check the full tower without disturbing it.
The tower is upright, but the green piece is slightly right of the tan board center. Reapproach its previous grasp for a small centering correction.
Regrasp the green piece, lift it slightly to avoid dragging, and shift it 18 mm left toward the tan board center.
Lower and release the recentered green piece, then lift clear of the full tower with the gripper open.
The full tower remains upright and centered after release. Retract the left arm clear of it and begin a gradual elbow-up return to origin.
Continue returning the open left gripper toward origin along a smooth path outside the completed tower.
Finish the smooth return to the original resting poses with both grippers open; the eight-piece tower remains upright and centered.
